verdict: AVOID new textile-trading exposure in Surat until the November 1 labour stir resolves and unit-level cash discipline is proven; lend only to established traders with clean stock statements and no wage arrears.
title: Surat textile trading: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Surat is the hub of the synthetic textiles industry, and trading here means buying grey and finished fabric from power-loom and embroidery units and moving it to garment makers and exporters [2]. Cash turns on stock and receivables, not on machines: fabric-making working capital is driven by inventory holding and receivables [8], and the weaving side is fixed- as well as working-capital intensive [9]. **So when a proposal lands, check the stock-and-receivables cycle first; if the buyer asks for a limit above what his own turnover supports, ask for the last twelve months of stock statements and debtor ageing.**

## What has broken now
Labour is the live risk, not demand. Embroidery workers across Surat units are threatening a protest march on November 1 over working hours, overtime wages and weekly offs, after an August 16 demonstration in Amroli turned violent and spread across the city [2]. Workers were fired for demanding a weekly day off, and shifts run 12 hours with three days off a year at most [1]. **So when a proposal lands, check whether the unit has wage arrears or pending overtime dues; if yes, ask for the labour settlement before sanctioning.** The November stir threatens sales in the Diwali pickup [2]. Note that source [3] on demonetisation is old and not usable for today's call.

## Where the growth is
Gujarat GST collections rose 11.9% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], a genuine local tailwind. Peer results are mixed but show margin room: KPR revenue grew 18.9% YoY with EBITDA margin of 25.7% [5], and Raymond Lifestyle posted 14.4% EBITDA margin in Q3FY26 [7]. **Pursue established Surat traders with diversified buyer bases and export order books; avoid pure job-work intermediaries and units with a single buyer.** Cotton prices are expected to stay reasonably firm on a 3%-4% gap for one to two years [4], which supports fabric realisations.

## How to grow safely
Structure limits against stock and receivables, not against turnover. **Take stock statements and debtor ageing every month, and a wage-compliance declaration every quarter.** Keep tenors short; the repo is 5.5% and the stance is tightening [D], so pricing must reflect that. **If a borrower cannot produce monthly stock statements, decline.**

## Early-warning signs
- Weekly: wage-payment status -> any delay, freeze fresh limits.
- Monthly: stock statement vs limit utilisation -> over-utilisation beyond agreed margin, ask for explanation.
- Monthly: debtor ageing -> any single buyer above 30% of receivables, seek diversification.
- Quarterly: GST filings vs sales declared -> mismatch, reassess.
watch: Any wage arrears or overtime default -> stop fresh disbursement and seek labour settlement proof
Utilisation above drawing power -> demand stock reconciliation before next limit
Single buyer above 30% of receivables -> ask for buyer-wise sales and diversification plan
Mismatch above tolerance -> reassess limit and seek explanation
Fresh protest or FIR at borrower unit -> suspend new limits until operations resume
